title: Relational Schema Design, Keys & Normal Forms (1NF–3NF)
summary: Understand Primary Keys, Foreign Keys, constraints, and step-by-step Normalization preventing update anomalies and duplicate data.
learningObjectives: Enforce data integrity directly in DDL using PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, NOT NULL, and CHECK constraints
Normalize messy repeating tables safely through 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF

sections.heading: 1. Relational Keys & Preventing Data Anomalies
sections.content:
Relational databases prevent duplicate, contradicting data by modeling entities cleanly into normalized tables connected by Primary Keys (unique immutable row identifiers) and Foreign Keys (enforcing referential links between tables).

Normalization eliminates insertion/update anomalies systematically: **1NF** bans repeating comma-lists inside single cells; **2NF** eliminates non-key attributes depending on only half a composite key; **3NF** ensures every non-key attribute depends solely on 'the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key' (removing transitive dependencies like storing `department_head_phone` repeatedly on every `employee` row).

codeExamples.code:
[departments] (id PK, name UNIQUE, budget CHECK > 0)
      | 1
      |---< Many [employees] (id PK, department_id FK -> departments.id, email UNIQUE, salary)
      |
      +--- One clear source of truth: updating department budget updates ONCE!
codeExamples.explanation: Referential foreign keys separate entities cleanly so modifying department metadata never requires updating thousands of employee rows.

keyPoints: Put strict invariants (`NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE`, `CHECK (price >= 0)`) right inside database DDL—not just frontend UI forms!
Avoid nullable foreign keys unless relationships are genuinely optional.
commonMistakes: Storing tag arrays as comma-joined text `'python,sql'` inside one VARCHAR column, breaking indexed joins.

sections.heading: 2. Explicit DDL Constraints in PostgreSQL
sections.content: Declarative DDL constraints make illegal application states unrepresentable regardless of which script or microservice touches the database.

codeExamples.explanation: Unique composite constraints `(student_id, course_id)` stop duplicate enrollment race conditions cleanly at the engine level.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Strictly constrained normalized schema enforcing uniqueness and valid progress bounds (0–100)

keyPoints: Add `UNIQUE (student_id, course_id)` to join/bridge tables preventing silent double records.
commonMistakes: Omitting `CHECK` bounds and letting negative balances or `150%` completion slip into tables.

exercises.title: Normalize an Unstructured Order Table to 3NF
exercises.objective: Split repeating customer and product fields into normalized entities.
exercises.description: Refactor `OrdersRaw(order_id, customer_email, customer_city, items_csv, supplier_phone)` into clean normalized DDL tables up to 3NF.
instructions: Extract Customers, Orders, and OrderItems resolving 1NF repeating `items_csv`.
Include appropriate PRIMARY KEY, REFERENCES, and CHECK (qty > 0) constraints.
hints: Many-to-many order items split neatly into a bridge table referencing `order_id` and `product_id`.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Extracting Customers, Products/Suppliers, Orders, and OrderItems guarantees 3NF integrity with zero redundant string replication.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why does storing `'Python,SQL,Rust'` inside a single text column violate First Normal Form (1NF)?

options.text: 1NF mandates atomic single-valued columns without repeating lists packed inside a cell
Text columns cannot contain commas in PostgreSQL
SQL forbids VARCHAR types longer than 10 chars
Primary keys must always be integers

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Atomicity simplifies filtering, counting, and indexing individual skills cleanly.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What happens when inserting a row into `enrollments` referencing a `course_id` that does NOT exist in `courses`, given an active `FOREIGN KEY` constraint?

options.text: The database rejects the INSERT atomically, preserving referential integrity
A missing placeholder row gets auto-created silently
Foreign keys validate only on SELECT queries

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Foreign key constraints prevent orphan child records referencing nonexistent parents.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What prevents inserting a negative quantity directly via bugs in app code?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Database CHECK constraints guarantee numeric domain bounds across every writer.

recap: You built normalized 3NF tables armed with declarative PRIMARY, UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY, and CHECK protections.
